text.text_excerpt: So excited to be the first reviewer of this place! My coworker and I ordered delivery, and it may have been opening day but I'm not sure. KUDOS to the attention they gave to our food, their service, and our delivery. I will definitely order from them again... Plus hopefully if enough people order, they can afford to get their delivery guy a bike :-) Between us we all had the breakfast sandwich, side of hash browns, fried green tomatoes, side of grilled vegetables, and some kind of crack-filled app that really needs to be renamed "beignet fries". All of it was good. Want more? Read on: The brekky sandwich was very basic, but the biscuit was definitely homemade. The hash browns had no seaso...

This is such a welcoming place! We were having Sunday Funday in the Quarter when we passed this spot. The doors were wide open and the musicians told us to "come in!", so we did. This is a small bar, but I found it cozy. It was packed with what seemed like neighborhood regulars and everyone was enjoying themselves. As the name of the bar promises, there was a jazz band holding court in the corner playing some classic tunes. I can't vouch for the food, but the drinks are well priced especially considering you are in the middle of a "touristy" area.

So after leaving another establishment extremely unsatisfied we came upon Jazz. I was hungry and thirsty and it was the first place we saw. All I wanted was some breakfast. Was that too much to ask? My husband and I decided to try it. It couldn't be worse than their neighboring establishment. I ordered the breakfast biscuit with egg, cheese and bacon. I thought $6.50 was a little high for that, but it is New Orleans, so I was willing to pay it. When my plate came out, not only did I have a large breakfast biscuit, I also had a ton of potatoes! $6.50 was a great price for that. My husband and I shared it and still had some left. It was delicious. This biscuit was a tad burned at the bottom...
